newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Alleged British spy to be treated, tried in Russia.
newsitem.headline: Alleged British spy to be treated, tried in Russia.

text.p: Russian judges ruled on Wednesday that an official accused of spying for Britain should undergo psychiatric treatment, then go on trial.

A court official said the judges of the Moscow City Court agreed with prosecutors who say junior foreign ministry official Platon Obukhov is mentally unstable now but was sane at the time of the alleged crime.
It was not immediately clear how long his treatment would take.
Obukhov's parents and lawyer, Anatoly Kucherena, argue that he has been mentally unstable since childhood and is unfit to stand trial. Kucherena said he would appeal against the judges' decision.

A second secretary in the foreign ministry's prestigious North America Department and a writer of pulp spy thrillers on the side, Obukhov, 28, has been held since April 1996 on charges he was paid for information by agents of Britain's MI6 intelligence service.
He is charged with high treason, which under the Russian criminal code is punishable with up to 20 years in prison.
Interfax news agency quoted Kucherena as saying he would appeal to a higher court.
"Court hearings have been accusatory from the very beginning," he said, complaining that the judges had declined to accept documents attesting Obukhov was not mentally fit to stand trial.
